About Behavox: 
 Behavox is shaping the future for how businesses harness their most important raw material - data. Our mission is bold: Organize enterprise data into actionable information that protects and promotes the business growth of multinational companies around the world. 
 From managing enterprise risk and compliance to maximizing revenue and value, our data operating platform presents a widespread opportunity to build multilingual, AI/ML-based solutions that activate data for every function within a global enterprise. 
 Our approach is unique, and it’s validated by our customers who tell us to keep forging ahead because no one else is aggregating, analyzing, and acting on data to uncover opportunities or solve problems quite the way we are. 
 We are looking for fearless innovators who have an insatiable appetite for building what no one has built before. 
 This is a hybrid role with 1 day in the office. 
 About the Role: 
 The Senior HR Business Partner is an individual contributor responsible for partnering with US and Canada business leaders to execute people strategies that support organizational performance and growth. 
 The role applies strong business acumen and HR expertise to advise leaders on workforce planning, performance management, employee relations, and organizational effectiveness within the US and Canada client group, and covers this territory directly and in full. 
 Reporting to the Principal HR Business Partner, the Senior HR Business Partner partners with leaders to deliver people initiatives while ensuring alignment with global frameworks and applicable US and Canada employment requirements. 
 During the initial phase of the role, the Senior HR Business Partner works under close coaching from the Principal HR Business Partner while building full ownership of the client group; oversight reduces as competence across the remit is demonstrated. 
 The role supports workforce planning, organizational design, and post-merger workforce integration workstreams for its client group, executes assigned enterprise HR programs and projects, and independently manages moderate-to-complex employee relations matters, escalating matters of significant complexity, cross-jurisdictional exposure, or elevated organizational risk to the Principal HR Business Partner. 
 It uses workforce data and people metrics to inform recommendations for its client group, and may be asked to support the Principal HR Business Partner on workforce matters outside the US and Canada as the function's footprint grows. 
 What You'll Bring: 
 HR Business Partnering — Applies working knowledge of business priorities and workforce needs within the US and Canada client group to align people initiatives with business objectives and provide trusted advisory support to leaders and managers at all levels. 
 Workforce Planning and Organizational Support — Applies workforce planning methodologies and organizational design principles to support headcount planning, org changes, and business effectiveness within the client group, in line with the framework set by the Principal HR Business Partner. 
 Employment Law and Employee Relations (US & Canada) — Maintains working knowledge of US and Canadian employment legislation and regulatory frameworks, independently managing moderate-to-complex employee relations matters within those jurisdictions. Working knowledge of employment fundamentals in other jurisdictions (e.g., UK, EMEA, APAC) is desirable, as the role may be asked to support the wider HR Business Partner team outside its core territory. 
 Talent Management and Performance — Applies performance management, career development, and talent process knowledge to support capability development within the client group. 
 People Analytics — Uses workforce metrics, organizational data, and HRIS-derived reporting to evaluate trends and support evidence-based decisions within the client group. 
 What You'll Do: 
 HR Advisory — Provides sound, commercially informed HR guidance to leaders on moderate-to-complex workforce and talent challenges within the US and Canada client group, exercising judgment on approach and escalating matters that exceed this level's scope. 
 Employee Relations Case Management — Manages moderate-to-complex employee relations cases end-to-end within US and Canada employment frameworks, balancing legal compliance, business priorities, and employee experience. 
 People Program Delivery — Delivers and locally adapts HR programs (performance cycles, workforce planning inputs, career development processes) for the client group in line with enterprise standards. 
 Workforce Data Interpretation — Interprets workforce data and people metrics for the client group to identify trends and inform recommendations to leaders, including through periods of increased organizational scrutiny or governance rigor (e.g., audit readiness, compliance program maturation, or a prior employer's scale-up or pre-exit period). 
 Compensation Analysis — Applies compensation data and benchmarking to support pay recommendations, offer construction, and pay equity considerations for the client group, escalating matters requiring Principal-level or Total Rewards review. 
 What We Offer 
 The opportunity to work on a global, mission-critical AI platform alongside the best engineers and technologists across multiple geographies 
 A role with real ownership and impact, building complex systems at scale in an environment that values speed, experimentation, and technical excellence 
 A highly attractive benefits package, including competitive cash compensation, an equity award aligned with long-term value creation, and comprehensive health insurance for employees and their families 
 Modern, comfortable offices in Montreal/Toronto downtown, with an expectation of (hybrid) working from the office 1 day per week, reflecting our belief in strong in-person collaboration. 
 A generous time-off policy of 30 days annually, plus public holidays and sick leave, recognizing the importance of sustained high performance 
 About Our Process 
 We take Talent very seriously and we are building a community of extraordinary individuals working together in very high performing teams. We also know that the best Talent always has options so we believe that the process has to be a two way assessment - the company AND the candidate assessing the business needs alignment, the career next step alignment, and the cultural alignment. 
 During the process we will begin by exploring the core factors regarding salary and location along with core experience and skills and values alignment. We will then deep dive explore the critical technical competencies we have identified for the role, and then we will deep dive in behavioral competencies. 
 The most aligned candidate will then be asked to do a practical work task simulation activity so we can make sure that you will enjoy the kind of work the role requires, and this task will typically be presented and discussed with a group of colleagues and managers. Finally we will ask you to meet with a number of our senior leaders to make sure that you are making the most informed call possible. 
 Please note that: 
 We want to get to know you and have a genuine conversation, so the use of AI tools or assistance during live interviews is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification from the process. 
 Interviews may be recorded for internal review purposes to ensure fairness and enable collaborative hiring discussions within the team.

The Site Administrative Assistant is an integral member of Woodfibre LNG’s dynamic Operations team. The role provides comprehensive administrative and coordination support to help the Operations Manager and team work safely, efficiently, and effectively at the Woodfibre LNG site.
 The successful candidate will act as a central administrative point of coordination for team schedules and rosters, meetings and action tracking, travel and transportation, site access, onboarding, training coordination, correspondence, and administrative records. The role requires strong judgement, accuracy, discretion, and responsiveness in a fast-paced industrial setting where plans and priorities may change quickly.
 The successful candidate reports directly to the Operations Manager. This is a site-based position working a 7-days-on/7-days-off rotation, with 12-hour shifts.
 Key Responsibilities 
 The successful applicant will:
 Provide day-to-day administrative and coordination support to the site-based Operations, Maintenance and Engineering team members.
 Maintain Operations team schedules, duty coverage information, contact lists, organizational information, and rotational rosters, ensuring updates are accurate and communicated promptly.
 Support shift and rotation changes by coordinating approved schedule updates, identifying administrative impacts, and communicating revised arrangements to affected stakeholders.
 Coordinate meetings, including scheduling, invitations, rooms or virtual meeting arrangements, agendas, materials, attendance records, and logistical requirements.
 Record meeting minutes, decisions, and assigned actions; Book approved employee travel and coordinate ground and marine transportation in accordance with Company procedures and manager authorixation. 
 Maintain accurate arrival, departure, and transportation schedules and communicate relevant updates to employees, site contacts, transportation providers, and other stakeholders.
 Respond to itinerary changes, cancellations, delays, and other travel disruptions, escalating operational or cost impacts to the appropriate manager.
 Maintain supporting travel records and assist with the reconciliation of approved travel expenses, invoices, or related documentation in coordination with Finance and budget owners.
 Coordinate visitor access requests, site visits, orientations, inductions, transportation and host information with Security, HSS, site contacts, and other accountable teams.
 Coordinate new-hire onboarding schedules and coordinate site mobilization activities with, Human Resources, IT, Security, HSS, Facilities, and other stakeholders.
 Coordinate badge, system-access, workspace, equipment, and other onboarding requests, while ensuring approvals and access decisions remain with the accountable functions. 
 Maintain organized shared drives, folders, administrative files, team records, and distribution lists in accordance with Company filing, privacy, retention, and access requirements.
 Prepare, proofread, and format correspondence, meeting materials, notices, schedules, reports, presentations, and other administrative documents.
 Retrieve and organize administrative records to support audits, assurance activities, internal reviews, and management requests.
 Receive and route general site and Operations enquiries, maintaining professional, timely, and service-oriented communication.
 Maintain effective handover notes at the end of each rotation so open actions, schedule changes, visitors, travel issues, and priority items remain visible and are progressed without interruption.
 Handle employee, travel, access, and operational information with appropriate confidentiality and discretion.
 Follow all Company HSSE requirements and site work practices and promptly report hazards, incidents, or concerns.
 Identify opportunities to improve administrative processes, standardization, information accuracy, coordination, and service delivery.
 Perform other duties within the scope of the role, as assigned.
 Required Experience and Qualifications: 
 At least five years of progressively responsible site administration, operations administration, project administration, or comparable coordination experience.
 Diploma or certificate in business administration, office administration, or a related discipline is preferred; an equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
 Experience supporting an industrial, construction, energy, natural resources, manufacturing, utilities, remote-site, or other operational environment is preferred.
 Demonstrated experience coordinating complex travel, workforce rosters, schedules, meetings, and changing logistical requirements.
 Advanced proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, particularly Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
 Experience using travel-booking, roster, scheduling, expense, document-management, learning-management, or site-access systems.
 Strong minute-taking, document formatting, proofreading, records organization, and action-tracking skills.
 Experience supporting onboarding, training coordination, visitor access, and cross-functional administrative processes.
 Ability to maintain accurate records and work effectively with confidential employee and business information.
 Skills and Competencies: 
 Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to coordinate multiple deadlines, schedules, and stakeholders without losing accuracy.
 Strong judgement and initiative, including the ability to identify urgent operational matters, resolve routine issues independently, and escalate appropriately.
 Clear and professional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with frontline employees, managers, contractors, service providers, and visitors.
 Calm, adaptable, and service-oriented when responding to last-minute travel changes, schedule disruptions, competing priorities, or time-sensitive requests.
 Demonstrated discretion, professionalism, and respect for confidentiality.
 Collaborative approach and ability to build effective working relationships across Operations, Human Resources, HSS, IT, Security, Facilities, Finance, and external providers.
 Commitment to safe work, accountability, reliable follow-through, continuous improvement, and effective rotational handovers.
 Additional Requirements: 
 This is a site-based position working a 7-days-on/7-days-off rotation with 12-hour shifts.
 Ability and willingness to travel to and from the Woodfibre LNG site by marine vessel and comply with applicable transportation and site-access requirements.
 Ability to work in an active industrial and construction environment and comply with all site orientation, personal protective equipment, security, and HSSE requirements.
 Flexibility to provide occasional support outside scheduled hours when required to address urgent travel, access, or operational coordination needs.
 A valid driver’s license.
 Must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
 Salary range: CAD 60,0 00 - 68,000 /yr

Huawei Canada has an immediate internship opening for a Researcher. 
 About the team: 
 Founded in 2012, the Noah’s Ark lab has evolved into a prominent research organization with notable achievements in academia and industry. The lab’s mission focuses on advancing artificial intelligence and related fields to benefit the company and society. Driven by impactful, long-term projects, the aim is to enhance state-of-the-art research while integrating innovations into the company's products and services, including LLMs, RL, NLP, computer vision, AI theory, and Autonomous driving. 
 About the job: 
 Assist in proposing and exploring novel research ideas to improve the efficiency and scalability of large language models. 
 Participate in applied research projects focused on enabling long-context LLMs, including work on efficient architectures, data curation, and post-training methods. 
 Collaborate on end-to-end projects by designing and executing experiments, analyzing results, and presenting findings. 
 Publish research in top-tier machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) conferences. 
 Track advances across the LLM and AI ecosystem, translating new developments into actionable insights for the team. 
 About the ideal candidate: 
 Currently pursuing a Ph.D. or Masters in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field. 
 A deep understanding of NLP and large language model (LLM) fundamentals and state-of-the-art methods, coupled with a strong theoretical grounding in machine learning. 
 Expertise in modern LLM architectures, including transformer models (e.g., Llama, Qwen) and good knowledge in linear-attention models (e.g., GDN, Mamba, GLA). 
 Strong programming skills in Python with expertise in PyTorch. Experience in training and evaluating LLMs. 
 Familiarity with diffusion models is an asset. 
 Excellent oral and written communication skills. Ability to work in a collaborative, research-oriented environment 
 Huawei aims to support a French-speaking work environment for its employees in Quebec. We have taken steps to avoid requiring a language other than French for this position. However, proficiency in English is essential for this role for the following reasons: 
 The person will be required to communicate regularly with colleagues located outside Quebec, where English is the primary language used for communication between offices. In addition, the nature of the tasks related to this position, which falls within a highly specialized field of artificial intelligence, also requires knowledge of English.

 An overview of this role 
 As the Director of Dedicated Infrastructure Engineering & Platforms, you will lead the engineering organization responsible for GitLab Dedicated, GitLab's premium single-tenant SaaS offering for enterprise customers in regulated industries, and public sector.
 You will lead a high-performing organization of managers and engineers who own the entire lifecycle of dedicated and cellular platforms, from orchestration, integrations, resilience, and incident response to switchboard APIs, public sector compliance, and enterprise customer migrations. Your mission is to scale GitLab Dedicated from its current trajectory toward an aggressive growth target, ensuring enterprise customers experience full platform capabilities with dedicated infrastructure, compliance certifications, and enterprise-grade SLAs in an isolated environment.
 As a high-impact executive leader, you will define the strategy for single-tenant and public sector SaaS platforms, drive critical infrastructure investments, ensure FedRAMP/compliance operational readiness, and build the switchboard and migration capabilities that allow enterprise customers to seamlessly transition to and scale on Dedicated. You will succeed by cultivating a culture of operational excellence, closing key business and roadmap gaps, and leading distributed engineering teams to deliver high-availability, highly secure platform experiences.
 What you'll do 
 Own the strategy and roadmap for GitLab Dedicated, and ensure the platform scales with customer growth and converges with GitLab's cellular architecture.
 Partner with Product and executive leadership to deliver on growth targets, with a focus on platform reliability, faster customer onboarding, infrastructure cost efficiency, and self-service administration.
 Lead the engineering teams that build and run the platform: tenant orchestration and integrations, resilience and incident response, the Switchboard control plane, public sector platforms and compliance, and enterprise migrations and import tooling. Uphold enterprise-grade SLAs across every tenant.
 Deliver GitLab Dedicated for Government: AWS GovCloud infrastructure, FedRAMP operations and audit readiness, air-gapped isolation, and public sector feature delivery.
 Make enterprise migrations to Dedicated predictable, repeatable, and low-disruption through self-service tooling and guided workflows.
 Hire, coach, and scale engineering managers across distributed teams, and bring practical AI-enabled workflows into how the organization works.
 Partner with Product, Security, and Customer Support to keep customer commitments, architecture, and investments aligned.
 What you'll bring 
 You have led engineering organizations that run enterprise single or multi tenant SaaS infrastructure and cloud platforms at scale.
 You have measurably improved production reliability, reduced toil, or lowered infrastructure cost on a platform you owned.
 You have deep expertise in cloud-native and cellular architectures, Infrastructure as Code, and modular services that deploy and scale independently across cloud environments.
 You have delivered and operated enterprise offerings under strict compliance regimes such as FedRAMP and AWS GovCloud.
 You have led organizational changes, including adopting AI enabled workflows that raise engineering system efficiencies.
 You translate financial targets into engineering investments, headcount plans, and execution roadmaps.
 You lead with ownership, speed with quality, and a focus on customer outcomes.
 About the team 
 The Dedicated Infrastructure & Platforms organization builds and runs GitLab Dedicated, our single-tenant enterprise SaaS offering, for GitLab's most strategic enterprise and public sector accounts. It is organized into five focus areas:
 Platform Orchestration & Integrations: orchestration, deployment, and environment automation for Dedicated tenants and cellular environments, plus integrations with external products.
 Core Features, Resilience & Response: compliance and operations driven features, disaster recovery, automated failover, rate limiting, and incident response automation.
 Switchboard & Control Plane: the APIs, tenant change automation, and operator and customer interfaces that make Dedicated self-service.
 Public Sector Platforms & Compliance: AWS GovCloud infrastructure, FedRAMP compliance operations, air-gapped isolation, and Geo replication for GitLab Dedicated for Government.
 Enterprise Migrations & Import Tooling: customer migration programs and playbooks, Geo-based migration tooling, Direct Transfer, and self-service guided import workflows.

KittySpout / DoggySpout is looking for a hands-on CRO Lead to join our team! You will own every conversion test across our site, landing pages, paid-acquisition funnels, on-site offers and post-purchase upsells. This is an all-in-one role: you set the strategy and you do the work – building the backlog, briefing and QA-ing tests, launching them and shipping the winners.
 We spend $2,000,000+ per month on Meta , so your tests reach significance fast. We are looking to hire someone with 3–4+ years running CRO programs for Shopify DTC brands. The ideal candidate has deep hands-on Intelligems experience, has built and tested paid-acquisition funnels, and can show the data behind tests that lifted conversion rate, AOV or revenue per visitor.
 The mission of this role
 Own every conversion test on both of our brands (site, landing pages, funnels, on-site offers and post-purchase upsells) so each visitor is worth more every month. Success is a steady, well-run test program that lifts conversion rate, AOV and revenue per visitor across every page, funnel and offer.
 Who are we?
 KittySpout is a premium DTC brand selling stainless steel cat water fountains, filters and accessories. We sell across Shopify, Amazon and Chewy, and we're one of the fastest-growing brands in the pet space – $50M+ in annual revenue and scaling to $100M+. We recently launched DoggySpout, expanding into an entirely new vertical and customer base. We're a 100% remote, lean, senior team that moves fast, and every person here has a massive impact on the business.
 What is our culture like & who is a good fit?
 Culture-fit is our #1 factor when hiring! We have a genuine will-to-win. No work is beneath us if it moves us towards our goals. We use creativity to do more with less – and quickly. We use data to make decisions and live by four core values:
 Better Everyday – keep a live test on each brand, write down the learning from every result, and improve the test plan, QA checklist and agency process after every round.
 Speed Is King – move from idea to live test in days, call finished tests on time, ship winners the week they win, and flag a conversion drop the same day.
 Work Smart – AI and automation first. Use Claude to turn Clarity recordings, reviews and surveys into test ideas and draft test briefs; automate reporting and drop alerts.
 Overdeliver – catch a conversion problem before anyone asks, bring the cause and the fix, and reuse winning patterns across both brands without being told.
 If you want a stress-free corporate 9–5 job, this isn't it. 
 If you want to challenge yourself and shape a fast-growing company, work directly with the founder, and play a big role in scaling it to $100M+... If you want to drive results with a group of passionate, smart, hardworking people, in an environment without politics or corporate chicanery, being hands-on and active – then you've come to the right place.
 Outcomes (what success looks like)
 90-day targets for each outcome are agreed with you before your start date.
 Conversion rate and revenue per visitor rise on both brands – measured weekly by brand (Intelligems, Shopify)
 Paid-acquisition landing pages and funnels that convert – CVR and RPV per funnel (Intelligems, Northbeam)
 Continuous improvement across the website – tests live every week; winners shipped
 AOV and post-purchase upsell take rate rise – AOV (Shopify), upsell take rate (AfterSell)
 No conversion drop goes unnoticed – drops caught and raised the same day
 Key Objectives
 Own the CRO test plan and backlog for both brands, ranked by expected impact, so the biggest wins run first.
 Build, test and launch paid-acquisition funnels, on-site offers and post-purchase upsells.
 Brief, QA and launch tests every week – then call results honestly and ship the winners.
 Drive measurable lifts in conversion rate, AOV and revenue per visitor.
 Catch conversion drops the same day and bring the cause and the fix.
 Manage our CRO agency and decide with the Head of Growth when work moves in-house.
 Report CRO KPIs weekly and run the weekly CRO & Funnels meeting.
 Fully remote, full-time
 Fluent in English
 CRO Experience: 3–4+ years running CRO programs for Shopify DTC brands is a must.
 Proof of Results: A record of tests and funnels that lifted CVR, AOV or RPV – with the data to back it up.
 Funnels: Experience building and testing paid-acquisition funnels and landing pages.
 Tools: Deep hands-on Intelligems experience, plus AfterSell (or similar), Microsoft Clarity and Shopify analytics. You can set up and QA a test without help.
 Briefing & Agencies: Experience briefing developers and designers, and managing a CRO agency.
 Experiment Design: You write clear hypotheses, size tests properly and call results on an agreed significance rule.
 Offer Sense: You know how bundles, discounts, subscriptions and upsells change conversion, AOV and margin.
 No issue working overtime or on the weekends if needed. You are passionate about your work.
 Excellent cultural fit as per our values above.
 Excited to play a big role in scaling the company and work closely with the founder.
 Bonus points: subscription or pet brand experience.

 Organization 
 Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a registered, charitable organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community-based primary care, wellness services, and health education to Durham community members who face multiple barriers to their health and well-being.

We always place every client at the centre of our approach to care, based on their needs. We address these needs through integrated clinical and wellness care and health education.

About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About the Role

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement.

In this role, you will:

 - Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

 - Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

 - Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

 - Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

 - Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

 - Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

 - Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

 - Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

 - Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

 - Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

 - Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

 - Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

 - Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

 - Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

 - Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

 - Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

 - Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

 - Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable.

 - Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

 - Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries.

 - Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring.

 - Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done.

 - Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed.

 - Are excited to use OpenAI’s products, agents, and emerging AI capabilities to transform how technical support operates at scale.

 Casual | Employee or Independent Contractor | Flexible Scheduling | Toronto and Central Region 
 The Care Company is a home healthcare organization dedicated to creating A Better Life for Those at Home . We support clients of all ages to live safely, independently, and with dignity in the comfort of their own homes. Our mission is to help people Make Each Day Count by delivering exceptional, person-centred care that puts people first and strives to be Better Today than we were yesterday.
 We are seeking a passionate and experienced Occupational Therapist (OT) to join our community rehabilitation team. This role is ideal for an OT who enjoys the autonomy of managing their own community caseload while being supported by an experienced interdisciplinary team.
 This is a flexible, casual opportunity that can be structured as either an employee or independent contractor position , depending on the successful candidate’s preference. Whether you are looking to supplement an existing caseload, build your community practice, transition into community care, or simply enjoy the flexibility of accepting referrals that fit your schedule, we would love to hear from you.
 You will work closely with clients and their families in the home, completing comprehensive assessments, developing individualized treatment plans, and recommending equipment and environmental modifications that promote safety, independence, and quality of life. Many of the individuals we support are living with complex or chronic medical conditions and require Alternate Level of Care (ALC) services.
 This is an exciting opportunity to join The Care Company as we continue to build and expand our Occupational Therapy program . We are looking for therapists with an entrepreneurial mindset who are excited to help shape the future of community rehabilitation. Beyond delivering exceptional clinical care, there will be opportunities to contribute to new service development, Requests for Proposals (RFPs), quality improvement initiatives, and innovative models of care that can help expand Occupational Therapy services across the community.
 As our OT program continues to evolve, there will also be mentorship and leadership opportunities for therapists interested in helping shape the future of community Occupational Therapy. This includes opportunities to mentor Occupational Therapy students during community placements, support the development of future clinicians, assist with onboarding new therapists, and contribute to clinical resources and best practices.
 Who This Role Is Perfect For 
 This opportunity may be a great fit if you are:
 An Occupational Therapist looking to supplement your existing caseload or practice.
 Interested in working as either an employee or independent contractor.
 Looking for greater flexibility and autonomy over your schedule.
 Passionate about helping clients remain safe and independent in their homes.
 Interested in mentorship, leadership, and supporting future Occupational Therapists.
 Entrepreneurial-minded and excited by the opportunity to help build and grow an evolving community rehabilitation program.
 Comfortable working independently while knowing clinical and operational support is available when needed.
 What You’ll Do 
 As an Occupational Therapist with The Care Company, you will have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in clients’ lives while enjoying the autonomy and flexibility of community practice. Working collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team, you will:
 Complete comprehensive in-home assessments within the required referral timeframe, including functional assessments, mobility evaluations, falls risk assessments, equipment needs, and ADL/IADL evaluations.
 Develop individualized, evidence-based treatment plans that empower clients to maximize independence, safety, and quality of life in their own homes.
 Provide follow-up visits focused on functional goal progression, mobility, environmental modifications, home safety, cognitive and physical strategies, and caregiver education.
 Recommend, trial, and prescribe assistive devices, adaptive equipment, and home modifications, collaborating with vendors and contractors where required.
 Support clients and families through education, coaching, and practical strategies that promote confidence, independence, and successful aging in place.
 Collaborate closely with nurses, physiotherapists, Personal Support Workers, physicians, care coordinators, case managers, and Ontario Health atHome to support seamless care transitions.
 Coordinate equipment procurement and assist with ordering supplies through Ontario Health atHome vendors.
 Monitor client outcomes and modify treatment plans as clinically appropriate to support meaningful, measurable progress.
 Maintain accurate, timely, and clinically sound documentation.
 Communicate proactively with the office regarding caseload availability, scheduling changes, and urgent referral readiness.
 Independently manage your caseload and schedule while receiving administrative, scheduling, clinical, and technical support from The Care Company.
 Deliver compassionate, ethical, and evidence-informed care while upholding The Care Company’s commitment to clinical excellence.
 Beyond Clinical Care 
 This role offers more than a traditional community caseload. As The Care Company continues to expand its Occupational Therapy services, you may also have opportunities to:
 Help shape and grow our community Occupational Therapy program.
 Contribute to new service development and Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
 Participate in quality improvement and innovative models of community care.
 Mentor Occupational Therapy students during community placements and help develop the next generation of OTs.
 Support the onboarding and mentorship of future Occupational Therapists joining the organization.
 Collaborate with leadership on the development of clinical resources, processes, and best practices.
 Grow into future clinical leadership and mentorship opportunities as our rehabilitation program expands.
 Scheduling 
 Flexible, casual scheduling with no fixed weekly schedule.
 Accept referrals based on your availability and geographic preference.
 Initial in-person home assessments are generally expected within 48–72 hours of receiving a visit request within your geographic service area.
 Ability to independently manage scheduling and communicate promptly with the office regarding availability.
 Toronto and Central Region may include Toronto, North York, Markham, Newmarket, Thornhill, and surrounding communities .
 Travel between client homes is required; access to a reliable vehicle is considered an asset.
 Qualifications and Experience 
 Registered and in good standing with the College of Occupational Therapists of Ontario (COTO) .
 Experience providing home and community care, particularly with HCCSS and/or Ontario Health atHome clients , is strongly preferred.
 Community Occupational Therapy experience and/or hospital discharge and transition-planning experience will also be considered.
 Demonstrated skill in functional assessments, equipment recommendations, safety evaluations, ADL/IADL retraining, and caregiver education in the home environment.
 Experience with equipment and supply ordering through Ontario Health atHome vendors is an asset.
 Strong understanding of community discharge planning, falls prevention, mobility supports, and caregiver training.
 Strong electronic documentation skills.
 Experience coordinating with interdisciplinary teams and communicating with case managers.
 Ability to work independently in the community and produce clear, timely, clinically appropriate documentation.
 Valid driver’s licence and access to reliable transportation, or the ability to travel efficiently within the designated service area.

 Compensation

 $75 per in-person follow-up visit. 
 $50 per virtual follow-up visit. 
 $25 per 30 minutes of approved administrative time completed outside of scheduled client visits, including documentation, care coordination, report writing, supply ordering, funding applications, and other client-related administrative duties.

 Flexible, casual scheduling – accept referrals based on your availability without being tied to a fixed weekly schedule.
 Autonomy to build and manage your own community caseload while being supported by an experienced interdisciplinary team.
 Competitive compensation , including paid administrative time for work completed outside of direct client visits.

 Opportunities to contribute to RFPs, new programs, quality improvement initiatives, and innovative models of community rehabilitation .
 Mentorship opportunities with Occupational Therapy students and future clinicians.
 Opportunities for future clinical leadership and program development.
 24/7 clinical support from experienced clinical leadership whenever guidance is needed.
 24/7 technical support for documentation and technology-related questions.
 Educational training and ongoing professional development opportunities.
 PPE provided.

About Fullscript 
 We’re an industry-leading health technology company on a mission to help people get better. We started in 2011 with one simple idea. Make it easier for practitioners to access the products they trust so they can deliver better care.
 That simple idea grew into a platform that powers every part of care. Today, more than 125,000 practitioners use Fullscript for clinical insights, lab interpretations, patient analytics, education, and access to high-quality supplements. Over 10 million patients rely on Fullscript to stay connected to their care plans and follow through on treatment.
 We build tools that make care smarter and more human. Tools that save time, simplify decisions, and help practitioners stay closely connected to the people they care for. When everything they need is in one place, they can focus on what matters most: helping people get better. 
 This is your invitation. 
 Bring your ideas, your grit, and your care for people.
Join us and shape the future of care.
 The Opportunity 
 The Senior Technical Writer owns documentation for one or more product areas of the Fullscript platform, and partners on the content strategy behind how the Support Center as a whole is structured. It has grown alongside a platform that evolves quickly. Expect a mix of mature documentation to maintain and refine, and newer product surfaces where you decide what should exist at all.
 This role reports to the Manager, Support Documentation, and is a primary partner on content strategy. You are comfortable deciding how content is structured so people can find it, where the line falls between self-service and a conversation with a support agent, which numbers the work should move, and what to stop doing. The work stays hands-on. You will keep writing and editing documentation alongside the structural work.
 The Support Center is the source of truth for platform knowledge, whether the reader is a practitioner, a patient, or one of our own support agents. An error in it reaches every audience at once, and content has to hold up for someone scanning a page as much as for a system pulling a single answer out of it.
 What you'll do 
 Documentation ownership 
 Own the content lifecycle for your product areas, from planning and drafting through maintenance and retirement, across every audience those areas touch.
 Document complex platform behavior, including integrations, identity and permissions, and net-new features with no existing content model to build on.
 Answer the question the reader arrived with, and where it genuinely helps, surface the adjacent capability they did not know existed.
 Use AI-assisted authoring to draft, summarize, and audit, then validate the output against the product before it publishes.
 Information architecture and content strategy 
 Partner with the Manager, Support Documentation, to design and evolve the information architecture of the Support Center: taxonomy, content types, navigation, and the metadata schema underneath them.
 Identify when a new feature makes existing documentation inconsistent or redundant, and lead the consolidation rather than layering new content on top.
 Monitor documentation effectiveness through self-service resolution, search performance, feature adoption, and support contact volume on documented topics, and prioritize work based on what those show.
 Produce AI-ready content: topics that still make sense when a system pulls one out on its own, consistent semantic markup, and metadata complete enough to route a question to the right answer.
 Use insights on where AI-assisted support returns wrong answers to prioritize the content fixes that follow, and negotiate that work against everything else in the queue.
 Release scoping and cross-functional collaboration 
 Gather and validate technical information ahead of a release, partnering with Product Management, Product Marketing, Engineering, and whichever subject matter experts (SMEs) own the detail, and translate what you learn into documentation.
 Work with support managers and frontline agents to find where customers get stuck, and use what they see to decide what gets documented and at what depth. Flag for Product when a pattern points at the product rather than the content.
 Produce an impact assessment for each release: which existing content becomes inaccurate, which audiences are affected, and who owns each open question.
 Identify what readers will need that the product specification does not address, and pursue those questions to an answer rather than documenting around the gap.
 Scope and size the releases nobody else can take yet, flag what will not fit early enough for someone to make a call, and grow the team's scoping until writers handle their own domains unaided.
 Standards, quality, and governance 
 Model and enforce the style guide, editorial policy, and content quality standard, and keep them current as the platform changes.
 Maintain consistent terminology across the Support Center: a controlled vocabulary of approved terms, the variants to avoid, and definitions SMEs have signed off on.
 Improve content operations: templates and content types, SME review and approval workflows, and a review cadence driven by risk, usage, and feedback rather than by article age.
 Govern the entire Support Center, including content the team does not author: taxonomy and metadata consistency, deduplication, and a defined path from published to deprecated to archived with redirects in place.
 Peer review and mentorship 
 Provide peer review and mentorship on craft, and be the editorial resource other writers come to.
 Bring other writers into release scoping and walk them through how you got to the impact assessment.
 What you bring to the table 
 5+ years writing technical or support documentation for SaaS platforms or complex software environments.
 Direct experience changing the structure of a documentation set, knowledge base, or help center, not only working within one.
 Strong writing skills, with the ability to turn complex technical behavior into accurate, scannable documentation, and to write the same information at the right depth for a practitioner, a patient, or a support agent.
 Comfortable working from incomplete information. You can define the documentation plan for a release that is still taking shape instead of waiting for a finished brief.
 Experience with content modeling and single-sourcing, so a fact lives in one place rather than being maintained across a dozen articles.
 Proficiency in a modern content management system, including its structured fields and metadata rather than only its authoring view.
 Comfort with AI-assisted authoring, and an interest in why a well-written article can still produce a wrong answer. 
 Bonus if you have 
 Healthcare, clinical, or other regulated software documentation experience.
 Experience with knowledge management practices where support agents contribute and improve content as they resolve cases.
 Experience improving how content gets found, through on-site search relevance, query analysis, or external ranking.
 Documenting integrations across a partner ecosystem, where behavior differs from one integration to the next.
 Experience with a component content management system (CCMS) such as Paligo, Heretto, or IXIASOFT, or with structured authoring in DITA.
 Taxonomy or ontology work, including knowledge graphs and the entity relationships underneath them.
 Prior work grounding a knowledge base for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or an AI support assistant, including how you measured whether the answers came back right.
 Prompt design, or a working view of where AI-generated drafts reliably fall short. 
 What we can offer you 
 Remote-first flexibility to work where you work best, with Ottawa, Toronto, or Calgary preferred for this role. 
 Flexible PTO and competitive pay, because work-life balance matters 
 RRSP/401k match and competitive compensation packages to invest in your future 
 Premium benefits package with customizable coverage, paramedical services, and an HSA. 
 Fullscript discounts to save on high-quality wellness products 
 Continuous learning opportunities to grow your skills and career
 Compensation range

The range shown reflects base salary only. The range shown reflects base salary only. Additional incentives, perks, and benefits may be available as part of Fullscript’s total rewards package.
Final compensation depends on experience, skills, and location. We review pay regularly to stay aligned with market data and internal equity. Benefits and total rewards may vary by region.
 Why Fullscript

About Sidekick
 At Sidekick, we help people recover faster from injuries. Trusted by Olympic champions and everyday athletes, our products have been featured in Men's Health and Running Magazine . With 94% of users finding relief, we aim to be the go-to injury relief brand.
 The role
 A lot of performance creative work goes into creating demand that wasn't there. That's not the problem here. Our customer already wants what we sell. Their heel hurts every morning when they get out of bed, or their ankle rolls on uneven ground and they've stopped trusting it.
 What they don't believe is that this is the thing that finally works. They've already bought the insoles, done the stretches, and gone to physio twice. So you have to teach before you can sell, and you have to earn trust from someone who has been let down already. It's a harder brief than most, and a more interesting one.
 You'll write our paid social advertising and own angle development and testing, reporting to our Creative Director. Expect to ship around 15 briefs a week, a mix of net-new concepts and iterations on ads that are already working. Your week is writing, research, and feedback to editors.
 You don't need a physiotherapy background, but you do need to pick up a clinical concept quickly enough to explain it clearly and honestly in fifteen seconds of camera time.
 What you'll do
 Find new winning angles. Better creative is what lets us spend more, so we need a steady supply of ads that keep working as budgets grow.
 Open new audiences. Runners, older adults worried about falling, people on their feet all day. Each group buys for a different reason, and every one we crack opens up new demand.
 Get more life out of winners. Read the data weekly, iterate what's working, retire what's finished.
 Write the scripts. Short and long-form video, hooks that stop the scroll, dialogue that sounds like a real person. This is most of your week.
 Direct the edit. Brief and manage editors and creators so the idea survives production.
 Extend what wins. Take proven angles into landing pages and email.
 What we're looking for
 4+ years writing paid social ads that were judged on sales (not brand awareness, engagement etc.)
 Your ads have been responsible for over $100K+/month in ad spend (across all your ads, for a single brand). We'll ask you to walk us through it.
 Proof you can iterate on a winner. Plenty of people can write one good ad; we want someone who gets eight more out of it.
 You've opened a new audience before, and you can name the angle that got you in
 Excellent writing for spoken word, which is a different skill from writing for the page
 Strong direct response fundamentals: offer, mechanism, objection handling, proof
 Experience briefing editors or creators
 Health, fitness or medical device categories are a plus
 What we care about
 We want people who are ambitious and hold themselves to a high standard. They don't need to be managed closely, and want to be the best at their craft. The volume is real and the feedback is direct. In exchange you'll see more results in a year than most people see in three. If you're looking for something comfortable, this won't be the right fit for you.

 You’ll see the direct impact of your work on business results
 You’ll be held to a high bar, which means you’ll get better fast

 Comprehensive health benefits

Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik/, Ashby's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. This role is close to my heart because, as someone who can both design and code, it’s where I’ve always done my best work, but also where I was seen as a rebel and an outsider. I want folks like me to feel at home at Ashby, and so I made Design Engineering a formal role and department that works closely with me. Our first hire was over five years ago, and we’re doubling the team from five to over ten in the next year.

This role truly expects you to design and code. Design Engineer at Ashby isn’t just a Frontend Engineer with new branding, nor is it a Designer vibe coding prototypes. Combining excellence in both is where magic happens. I found that when I put my best effort into both the design and technical implementation of a feature, I had a nimbleness and creativity that was hard to achieve when I did only one or the other. For instance, the UX and UI I envisioned often influenced the data model's design and flexibility, while the understanding of technology's capabilities often simplified or improved the design. This role embraces that.

You’ll work on our most challenging design problems, help others improve their designs by expanding and enhancing our in-house design system, and consult on bespoke design work needed by Product Engineers. To ground it with examples, Design Engineers at Ashby have:

 - Redesigned our mobile web app by talking with customers who use it often, wireframing new flows, implementing its design system, and using that system to turn the wireframes into a polished UI.

 - Built a set of flexible, composable components in our design system that allow other engineers to build beautiful, consistent setup wizards across our product easily.

 - Helped a Product Engineer improve the information hierarchy and scannability of their design for viewing a candidate’s assessments. Recruiters can quickly parse information and pick out anomalies.

The Design Engineer role is more common today than five years ago, but I believe Ashby offers a unique opportunity that few can match:

 - You work on a product at scale, not at an early-stage startup struggling to find users and get feedback on what you’ve designed and built. At Ashby, your work will touch over 100,000 weekly active users, millions of candidates per week, and notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. You’ll get to test out ideas with our own recruiting team and hiring managers who use Ashby every day (like me), and often hear customer feedback as early as the day you release.

 - This role has always had the commitment of both Benji (CEO & Co-Founder) and me: I’ve held the role, steadfastly championed it since we started hiring in 2020, and haven’t diluted its responsibilities as we’ve grown (in fact, we’ve doubled down).

 - You get to shape the UI and UX of a powerful and complex product. Our users need software that helps them move quickly while adapting to their unique workflows and preferences. As a result, our UI isn’t a simple chatbox, but it can’t rely on a sea of knobs and dials either. It needs to feel approachable to someone using it for the first time while offering increasingly powerful ways to customize and automate their work.

 


WHY YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY

Design Engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some reasons you might not enjoy the role:

 - You only want to work on design systems. While improving our design system is one of many responsibilities, you won’t be able to work on it exclusively.

 - You like to do extensive research and user testing before implementation. The beauty of being part-Engineer is that you can build conviction by shipping to a subset of users (including our own team) and gathering feedback!

 - You want everything to be perfect before it gets into a user’s hands. One of the drivers of our success is that we ship fast. While we appreciate the strive for perfection, we also realize it doesn’t need to be achieved all at once; instead, we iterate over time, often letting user feedback and business needs drive prioritization.

 - You don’t have excellent taste and execution in visual design. Design Engineers set the bar for visual design in our app and continually improve it, pushing its boundaries with each new feature or redesign.

 - You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the design and technical details.

 - You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs.

 


WHAT SENIORITY/LEVEL TO APPLY FOR

We’ve posted levels from Junior to Staff. The higher the level, the more experience and alignment with the role we expect when reviewing your application and while interviewing. Please apply to the one that sets the right expectations.

 - Junior Design Engineer - You should have no more than 2 years of industry experience as a designer or engineer. We want to see projects (personal or professional) with at least a couple of users that showcase great visual taste and burgeoning talent in both UI/UX and Engineering.

 - Design Engineer (This Posting) - This posting covers both Mid and Senior levels. You have 2+ years of continuous experience (e.g., internships don’t count) as an Engineer or a Designer. You have good proficiency in both Design and Engineering, with exceptional proficiency in the discipline you practice full-time. Regardless of which discipline you’re coming from, we expect experience designing products and shipping code to hundreds of users (even if through side projects).

 - Staff Design Engineer - We’re looking for folks who’ve practiced our flavor of Design Engineering professionally. It may not be through a formal title, but you’ve made major contributions to a design system and designed and implemented features for hundreds of users and iterated on them through user feedback.

Internally, we do not use these titles, but Engineers are leveled based on proficiency (which you can read about here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/engineering/leveling-and-compensation).

 


WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

 


ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 


MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 


COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/d4679311-9dba-4031-bf5e-19ce78597ab1/calendar.png]
 

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

 


INCREASE LEVERAGE, NOT TEAM SIZE

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

 - Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

 - Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

 - AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/engineering/ai-ashby-engineering-and-the-future.

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/8d94727a-46d8-42a2-9627-ddcd7f822f95/arjun.png]
 

And a demo of one of these building blocks:




PUT EFFORT INTO DIVERSITY

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

 


WORK-LIFE BALANCE: IT’S A MARATHON, NOT A SPRINT

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives you a lot of flexibility in how you structure your days and weeks. In practice, that means you keep your own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching your feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and you actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school.  Mujda https://www.linkedin.com/in/mujdaalamzai/ (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article https://nextplayso.substack.com/p/should-you-join-ashby about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”

 


INTERVIEW PROCESS

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together through pair programming, designing, writing design system specs collaboratively, and discussing decisions. There are no leetcode or whiteboard exercises.

Our interview process is three rounds:

 - Introduction call with me (30m, live). Be prepared to screen-share examples of your work.

 - A second round where we either do a technical screen (1h, live) or a design take-home (~3h async, 30m live)

 - Three interviews, a deep dive into a past design system or design project, a design system interview, and the interview we didn’t do in the second round: technical screen or design take-home. (3h, live)

Depending on our leadership team’s bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.

I will be your main point of contact and prep you for interviews. Each round will have written guidance so you know what to expect. You’ll meet 3-4 people in Design Engineering (with 5-15 minutes in each interview to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback!

 


YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY

We want an exceptional onboarding experience for every new hire. At Ashby, your dev environment is set up with a single script, you push your first product change on day one, and you spend the rest of your time shipping product changes that give you a tour of our codebase and best practices. The product changes increase in scope and ambiguity from simple copy changes to the delivery of a prominent, impactful feature. Your manager will do a 30, 60, and 90-day review to give feedback and calibrate on how we work together.

It’s a team effort to get you successfully onboarded; you’ll have a peer paired with you to answer questions, pair program, and check in often to see if you need help. The rest of the team will run training sessions on our culture, product, engineering process, and technical architecture.

 


TECHNOLOGY STACK

Our tech stack is TypeScript (frontend & backend), React, GraphQL API, Node.js, Postgres, and Redis. Depending on the level you’re applying for and your past experience, we expect, at a minimum, good proficiency with TypeScript, React, and CSS. Proficiency with backend technologies is a plus, as it allows you to work without coordinating with Product Engineers.

 


BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

 - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 À PROPOS DE VALSOFT CORP.: 
 Fondée au Canada en 2015, Valsoft possède aujourd’hui un portefeuille mondial de plus de 118 entreprises.  DESCRIPTION DU POSTE: 
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) adjoint(e) administratif(ve) juridique proactif(ve), organisé(e) et soucieux(se) du détail pour soutenir les activités quotidiennes de notre équipe juridique. Ce poste convient particulièrement à une personne qui aime gérer plusieurs priorités, coordonner les activités avec différents intervenants et veiller à ce que les documents, dossiers, échéances et demandes administratives soient traités avec précision et efficacité.
 La personne retenue collaborera avec les équipes internes, les conseillers juridiques externes, les auditeurs, les prêteurs, les institutions financières, les fournisseurs et d’autres tiers. Il s’agit d’un rôle administratif qui ne nécessite pas de formation juridique officielle. Une expérience antérieure dans un environnement juridique, corporatif, de conformité, bancaire ou de services professionnels constitue un atout.
 RESPONSABILITÉS PRINCIPALES: 
 Dossiers corporatifs et gestion des entités 
 • Maintenir des renseignements exacts et à jour sur les sociétés et les entités juridiques, notamment leur statut, leurs administrateurs et dirigeants, leurs adresses commerciales, leurs numéros d’enregistrement et d’autres renseignements clés.

• Coordonner les modifications corporatives courantes et obtenir, au besoin, des extraits de registre, des certificats de conformité, des organigrammes et d’autres renseignements corporatifs.
 Signatures et gestion documentaire

• Organiser l’envoi, le retour et l’entreposage des documents originaux et tenir à jour les registres indiquant leur emplacement.
• Coordonner les copies certifiées conformes, les authentifications notariales, les légalisations et les apostilles, en assurant la liaison avec les demandeurs, les signataires et les parties chargées de la certification.
 Conseillers juridiques externes, factures et systèmes juridiques 
 • Ouvrir, surveiller et fermer les dossiers dans les logiciels de facturation juridique et effectuer les suivis nécessaires auprès des avocats internes et des conseillers juridiques externes concernant les dossiers en suspens ou inactifs.
